MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 62,418? (1 mark)
   A. 6,000
   B. 600,000
   C. 6
   D. 60,000

2. Which of these shows 190 in words? (1 mark)
   A. one hundred and nine
   B. two hundred and ninety
   C. nineteen
   D. one hundred and ninety

3. Which of these is a factor of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 9
   C. 5
   D. 8

4. What is the 8th multiple of 7? (1 mark)
   A. 56
   B. 63
   C. 49
   D. 15

5. Which of these is a factor of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 5
   C. 4
   D. 8

6. Work out 1,856 + 4,567. (1 mark)
   A. 6,433
   B. 5,313
   C. 6,323
   D. 6,423

7. Work out 4,236 + 1,528. (1 mark)
   A. 5,754
   B. 5,774
   C. 5,764
   D. 5,664

8. Work out 12 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 262
   B. 252
   C. 36
   D. 242

9. Which number is in the 9 times table? (1 mark)
   A. 71
   B. 72
   C. 74
   D. 75

10. What is 63 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 93
   B. 1,890
   C. 189
   D. 18,900

11. What is 65 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 23
   B. 14
   C. 12
   D. 13

12. Change 13/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/3
   B. 4 2/3
   C. 5 1/3
   D. 1 4/3

13. Beth writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 11/5
   B. 13/6
   C. 2/9
   D. 3 1/2

14. What is 1/3 of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 16
   B. 8
   C. 24
   D. 4

15. Write 7/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.07
   B. 0.7
   C. 7.0
   D. 0.17

16. Write 0.6 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1/6
   B. 60/10
   C. 6/10
   D. 6/100

17. Write 0.09 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 90/100
   B. 9/1000
   C. 9/10
   D. 9/100

18. Which expression shows "5 more than x"? (1 mark)
   A. x − 5
   B. 5x
   C. x ÷ 5
   D. x + 5

19. Otieno is a years old. His sister is 3 years older. Which expression shows his sister's age? (1 mark)
   A. a + 3
   B. a − 3
   C. 3a
   D. a ÷ 3

20. What is 75 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 0.075 m
   B. 75 m
   C. 7.5 m
   D. 0.75 m

21. What is 2 m 90 cm + 3 m 30 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 20 cm
   B. 5 m 20 cm
   C. 7 m 20 cm
   D. 6 m 10 cm

22. A rope 9 m 60 cm long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 2 m 40 cm
   B. 4 m 80 cm
   C. 9 m 56 cm
   D. 2 m 50 cm

23. Change 375 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 37 cm
   B. 4 m 75 cm
   C. 3 m 75 cm
   D. 4 m 25 cm

24. A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 24 cm
   B. 18 cm
   C. 12 cm
   D. 36 cm

25. A rectangle has an area of 45 square units and 9 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 36
   B. 6
   C. 5
   D. 54

26. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. Rectangle P
   C. Rectangle Q
   D. It cannot be told

27. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 48
   B. 72
   C. 6
   D. 5

28. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid A
   B. It cannot be told
   C. They are equal
   D. Cuboid B

29. How many quarter-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 4

30. What is 4 L − 1 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 2 1/2 L
   B. 2 3/4 L
   C. 2 1/4 L
   D. 2 L

31. A 50 kg sack of rice is packed into bags of 5 kg. How many bags are filled? (1 mark)
   A. 45
   B. 250
   C. 5
   D. 10

32. How many hours are in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 420 hours
   B. 192 hours
   C. 84 hours
   D. 168 hours

33. Wekesa wakes up at half past six in the morning. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 6:30 noon
   B. 6:30 a.m.
   C. 6:30 p.m.
   D. 6:03 a.m.

34. How many minutes are in 8 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 192 minutes
   B. 800 minutes
   C. 540 minutes
   D. 480 minutes

35. How many cents are in Ksh 40? (1 mark)
   A. 4,000 cents
   B. 140 cents
   C. 40,000 cents
   D. 400 cents

36. How many cents are in Ksh 25? (1 mark)
   A. 125 cents
   B. 25,000 cents
   C. 250 cents
   D. 2,500 cents

37. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with two equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 0

38. What should every good table have? (1 mark)
   A. No numbers
   B. A title and column headings
   C. A long story
   D. Only pictures

39. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many are football or swimming together? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 7

40. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many more are there of walking than of bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A school timetable shows assembly from 8:00 a.m. to 8:20 a.m. and mathematics from 8:20 a.m. to 9:10 a.m. Find how long each lasts and the total time. (4 marks)

42. Explain what the 0 in 4.05 shows and say how 4.05 is different from 4.5. (3 marks)

43. A classroom floor is covered with 15 rows of 10 tiles. How many tiles are used? If 6 tiles are broken and must be replaced, how many tiles are unbroken? (4 marks)

44. Ten pupils chose their favourite drink: 4 chose juice, 3 chose milk, 2 chose water and 1 chose tea. Write two facts that you can read from this data. (2 marks)

45. A bicycle costs Ksh 6,500, a helmet Ksh 1,750 and a lock Ksh 850. Find the total cost. (3 marks)

46. Work out 48 × 21 and check the answer by estimating first. (4 marks)

47. A farmer packs 84 mangoes equally into 4 baskets. How many mangoes are in each basket? Then he picks 3 more mangoes. Can he share all 87 mangoes equally among the 4 baskets? Explain. (5 marks)

48. Box P is 5 blocks long, 2 wide and 4 high. Box Q is 4 blocks long, 4 wide and 2 high. Which has the greater volume and by how many blocks? (4 marks)

49. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact product. (4 marks)

50. Write these times using a.m. or p.m.: (a) waking up at half past six in the morning, (b) school ending at a quarter past three in the afternoon, (c) supper at half past seven at night. (3 marks)

51. Explain why we add the numbers in the total row of a table. (3 marks)

52. A vendor sells 2 bags of maize (m) and 3 bags of beans (b) on Monday, and 4 bags of maize and 1 bag of beans on Tuesday. (a) Write an expression for Monday. (b) Write an expression for Tuesday. (c) Simplify the expression for the two days together. (5 marks)

53. Write 13.42 in expanded form and give the total value of the digit 4. (3 marks)

54. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. (a) How many lines of symmetry does it have? (b) How many right angles does it have? (c) Find its perimeter. (d) Say one way in which it is different from a square. (5 marks)

55. At what times on a clock do the hands make a right angle and a straight line? Give one example of each. (4 marks)

56. List four materials you could use to collect and record data about the types of vehicles that pass the school gate. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 60,000
   The digit 6 is in the ten thousands place, so its total value is 6 × 10,000 = 60,000.

2. D — one hundred and ninety
   190 = one hundred and ninety. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

3. D — 8
   24 ÷ 8 = 3 with nothing left over, so 8 is a factor of 24. The others leave a remainder.

4. A — 56
   Multiply 7 × 8 = 56. It is the 8th multiple of 7.

5. B — 5
   30 ÷ 5 = 6 with nothing left over, so 5 is a factor of 30. The others leave a remainder.

6. D — 6,423
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,856 + 4,567 = 6,423.

7. C — 5,764
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 4,236 + 1,528 = 5,764.

8. B — 252
   12 × 1 = 12 and 12 × 20 = 240. 12 + 240 = 252.

9. B — 72
   9 × 8 = 72. The digits of a multiple of 9 add up to 9: 7 + 2 = 9.

10. B — 1,890
   63 × 3 = 189, then × 10 gives 1,890.

11. D — 13
   5 × 13 = 65, so 65 ÷ 5 = 13.

12. A — 4 1/3
   13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/3, so 13/3 = 4 1/3.

13. D — 3 1/2
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 3 1/2.

14. B — 8
   24 ÷ 3 = 8 and 8 × 1 = 8. So 1/3 of 24 is 8.

15. B — 0.7
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 7/10 = 0.7.

16. C — 6/10
   The last digit of 0.6 is in the tenths place, so the denominator is 10. 0.6 = 6/10.

17. D — 9/100
   The last digit of 0.09 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.09 = 9/100.

18. D — x + 5
   The key words tell us the operation. "5 more than x" is written x + 5.

19. A — a + 3
   Older means add, so her age is a + 3.

20. D — 0.75 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 75 cm in metres is 0.75 m.

21. A — 6 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 290 + 330 = 620 cm = 6 m 20 cm.

22. A — 2 m 40 cm
   960 ÷ 4 = 240 cm = 2 m 40 cm.

23. C — 3 m 75 cm
   375 ÷ 100 = 3 remainder 75. So 375 cm = 3 m 75 cm.

24. A — 24 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.

25. C — 5
   Rows × columns = 45, so columns = 45 ÷ 9 = 5.

26. C — Rectangle Q
   P = 5 × 7 = 35 and Q = 6 × 6 = 36. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

27. D — 5
   Layers = 60 ÷ 12 = 5.

28. D — Cuboid B
   A = 10 × 2 × 2 = 40 blocks. B = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

29. D — 4
   Four quarters make one whole, so four 1/4 L containers make 1 L.

30. C — 2 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 4 L − 1 3/4 L = 2 1/4 L.

31. D — 10
   50 ÷ 5 = 10 bags.

32. D — 168 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 7 × 24 = 168 hours.

33. B — 6:30 a.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 6:30 a.m..

34. D — 480 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 8 × 60 = 480 minutes.

35. A — 4,000 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 40 = 40 × 100 = 4,000 cents.

36. D — 2,500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 25 = 25 × 100 = 2,500 cents.

37. A — 1
   Only one fold, from the top corner to the middle of the base, makes the halves match.

38. B — A title and column headings
   A title tells what the table is about and headings tell what each column shows.

39. A — 6
   5 + 1 = 6.

40. D — 4
   6 − 2 = 4.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Assembly 20 minutes, mathematics 50 minutes, total 70 minutes (1 hour 10 minutes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duration, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 1 h 10 min.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The 0 shows that there are no tenths. 4.05 is 4 ones and 5 hundredths; 4.5 is 4 ones and 5 tenths, which is bigger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of zero, 1 mark for each correct reading.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 150 tiles; 144 tiles unbroken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 15 × 10, 1 mark for 150, 1 mark for 150 − 6, 1 mark for 144.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: juice is the most popular with 4 pupils; only 1 pupil chose tea; 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils were asked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact based on the numbers.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 9,100
   Working / marking points: 6,500 + 1,750 = 8,250 (1 mark); 8,250 + 850 (1 mark); Ksh 9,100 (1 mark).

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 50 × 20 = 1,000. Exact: 48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960, so 1,008.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for each partial product and 1 mark for the sum 1,008.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: 21 mangoes in each basket. 87 ÷ 4 = 21 remainder 3, so he cannot share all 87 equally; 3 will be left over.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 21, 2 marks for 87 ÷ 4 = 21 R 3 with working, 1 mark for answering no, 1 mark for the explanation.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Box P, by 8 blocks
   Working / marking points: P = 40 (1 mark); Q = 32 (1 mark); P is greater (1 mark); 40 − 32 = 8 (1 mark).

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 40 × 20 = 800. Exact: 836.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding to 40 and 20, 1 mark for 800, 1 mark for 38 × 2 = 76 and 38 × 20 = 760, 1 mark for 836.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) 6:30 a.m. (b) 3:15 p.m. (c) 7:30 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct time with a.m. or p.m.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: To check that we have counted everything and that the total equals the number of items collected. If it is different we must count again.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for checking, 1 mark for comparing with the number collected, 1 mark for counting again.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2m + 3b (b) 4m + b (c) 2m + 3b + 4m + b = 6m + 4b
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c): 1 mark for adding the expressions, 1 mark for 6m, 1 mark for 4b.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10 + 3 + 0.4 + 0.02. The total value of 4 is 0.4 (4 tenths).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 10 + 3, 1 mark for 0.4 + 0.02, 1 mark for the total value of 4.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2 (b) 4 (c) 26 cm (d) Its sides are not all equal (only opposite sides are equal), and it has 2 lines of symmetry instead of 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 2 marks for (c) (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 with the answer and unit), 1 mark for (d).

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Right angle: 3 o'clock (or 9 o'clock). Straight line: 6 o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a right angle example and reason, 2 marks for a straight line example and reason.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: a pencil, an exercise book or paper, a ruler for drawing a table, a clipboard or hard book, a watch or clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible material.
